question.text: A speculative trade in derivatives is characterized by:

answer.text: No underlying position in cash, implementing a view on future prices at a lower cost
Simultaneously buying and selling to capture price differentials
Protecting an existing portfolio from adverse price movements
Providing continuous buy and sell quotes to ensure market liquidity

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 210, a speculative derivative trade is not supported by an underlying cash position; it implements a view on future prices at a lower cost. Pages 200-201 and 210 support the futures-margin and option-premium cost mechanics. The SEBI loss-study footnote on page 208 is consistent with the high-risk nature of speculative F&O trading. The Trap: Simultaneous buying and selling for price differentials describes arbitrage, not speculation. Protecting an existing portfolio is hedging. Providing continuous quotes describes market making. Note: Speculation is defined by the absence of an underlying cash position and the lower upfront cost (margin or premium) compared with taking the same view in the cash market.
